claims.text: Rapid thermal annealing facilitates formation of a hierarchical microstructure.
Rapid thermal annealing enhances long-range magnetic order.
A hierarchical microstructure with tuned long-range ordering and optimized domain boundaries reduces domain-wall pinning.
Magnetic domain structure and long-range ordering govern soft-magnetic properties, including coercivity.
Grain boundaries and other microstructural barriers can pin domain-wall motion.
Reducing barriers to domain-wall motion lowers coercivity and magnetic hysteresis.
Rapid thermal annealing produces refined grain structures and controlled magnetic-domain configurations.
Improved grain connectivity produced by rapid thermal annealing supports faster heat conduction.
Reduced domain-wall pinning produces a stronger magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Rapid thermal annealing can simultaneously enhance low-field magnetocaloric performance and reduce magnetic hysteresis.
Rapid thermal annealing will increase the isothermal entropy change or adiabatic temperature change relative to the baseline.
Rapid thermal annealing will produce faster heat exchange than conventional slow annealing or the as-cast condition.
Yield strength and ductility after rapid thermal annealing will remain comparable to or improve over the baseline.
As-cast or slow-annealed rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys typically have higher magnetic hysteresis and less-optimized thermal and mechanical properties.
Long-duration annealing can cause recrystallization and grain growth, and coarse grains can be associated with low yield strength.
The proposed intervention is rapid thermal annealing near 600°C for 120–240 seconds with controlled cooling.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to single-phase rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys of similar composition, such as FeCoNiMn-based systems made by sputtering or melt processing.
Applicability to alloys with significant secondary phases or substantially different compositions is uncertain.
The relevant magnetic-refrigeration operating range is approximately 100–300 K.

Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and enhanced low-field magnetocaloric response without degrading heat exchange or mechanical stability would falsify the hypothesis.
